question: Which documented Taiwan legal retrieval providers have enough endpoint, response contract, authentication, terms, privacy and removal evidence to be considered for a later runtime design?

providers.authentication: Platform account and password are exchanged for a six-hour token; JList and JDoc require the token.
providers.rate_or_availability: Documented service window is 00:00-06:00 daily; no numeric request-rate limit was found in the reviewed specification.
providers.terms_or_license: Official API specification and Judicial Yuan website open-data declaration were found; an API-specific production SLA and numeric rate contract were not found in the reviewed material.
providers.privacy_and_removal: A repeated JID means the later version replaces the earlier version. A documented removal response requires deletion of a previously downloaded judgment.

providers.operator: Taiwan High Prosecutors Office / Ministry of Justice
providers.authentication: No machine authentication contract was found in the reviewed public guidance.
providers.terms_or_license: The official guidance documents publication scope and says the data is for reference and the original document controls. It does not document an automation API contract.
providers.privacy_and_removal: Publication and redaction rules exist, but no machine removal event or synchronization contract was found.

response_contract: 14 named MCP tools are publicly listed
No version-pinned per-tool output schema was found in the reviewed public page
providers.authentication: The hosted public endpoint is described as no registration, no API key and no OAuth.
providers.rate_or_availability: No numeric rate limit or SLA was found in the reviewed public pages.
providers.terms_or_license: Hosted endpoint use instructions and privacy policy were found; a separate hosted-service terms document with a versioned output guarantee was not found.
providers.privacy_and_removal: Tool name, full query parameters, result status and processing time are logged for 90 days; full IP addresses are not stored. The service says it does not retain judgment copies and stops serving official records after source removal.

providers.authentication: Remote MCP documents OAuth dynamic registration. Public REST is described as no-key, with optional enterprise API keys.
providers.rate_or_availability: Terms say rate limits are published in API responses; no fixed numeric limit or availability SLA was found in the reviewed documents.
providers.terms_or_license: Hosted service terms permit individual, internal-business, research and professional use. Resale, corpus mirroring and training or fine-tuning on output require a separate agreement or are prohibited as stated.
providers.privacy_and_removal: The provider may log query text, timestamps, IP-derived metadata, result counts, connector identity and user agent. A retention period was not found in the reviewed documents.

response_contract: search_judgments documents success, query, total_count, results, cached and timestamp
get_judgment documents case fields, full text, source URL and history
providers.authentication: Local MCP process has no hosted provider authentication; upstream websites may impose their own controls.
providers.rate_or_availability: No centralized service SLA exists. The project describes best-effort maintenance and warns against bulk or high-frequency retrieval.
providers.terms_or_license: Code is MIT and the LawChat structured dataset is CC0. Users remain responsible for each upstream website's terms; centralized service deployment shifts responsibility to the builder.
providers.privacy_and_removal: Requests originate from the user's computer. Some upstream public records can contain personal data; the tool does not add redaction. Local cache, cookies and browser fallback require a separate security review.

review_findings.label: FACT
review_findings.finding: The five candidates are not interchangeable: one is an official authenticated REST feed, one is a public search UI, two are hosted MCP services, and one is a local scraper-backed MCP process.

review_findings.label: FACT
review_findings.finding: No reviewed candidate has all endpoint, immutable output schema, authentication, numeric rate, availability SLA, privacy retention and removal evidence needed for unattended production use.

review_findings.label: INFERENCE
review_findings.finding: A later design should separate discovery/search from official-document verification and must not use PSUE HTML as an undocumented API.

review_findings.label: UNKNOWN
review_findings.finding: The system owner has not selected a provider, accepted its terms, assigned credential ownership or approved failure and change-management rules.

minimum_conditions_before_approval: Select one discovery provider and one official verification path instead of treating all sources as fallbacks with equivalent authority.
Freeze the exact tool or REST request and response schema with contract fixtures before runtime code is written.
Approve query allowlists that exclude case narrative, names, addresses, identifiers and case numbers unless an official-source workflow expressly requires them.
Record authentication owner, secret storage, rate handling, timeout, retry, circuit-breaker and source-removal behavior.
Obtain HG-LR-02 privacy and security approval before any hosted provider receives a query.
Keep results as source evidence and candidate-analysis input with HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, never as a legal conclusion.
